findings.title: readSequence loops forever or misbehaves on indefinite-length or truncated input
findings.body: readLength() returns -1 for the indefinite-length form (0x80). readSequence() then skips the `while (length > 0)` loop and returns an empty list without reading anything. For malformed input the loop depends on readNext() consuming data. A zero-length element can make no progress. The caller only checks `seq.size() != 2`, so malformed signatures yield confusing errors instead of a clear rejection. Short-form lengths are also not validated against the remaining stream size.

findings.title: Dead duplicate ASN1 encoding calls
findings.body: Lines 114-115 create encoders and write r and s, then discard the result. The same values are encoded again in the return statement. This is leftover code that does useless work.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns a non-BC provider
findings.body: The method returns the provider of the default KeyStore type, which is SUN. It is not BouncyCastle. Callers such as BouncyIntegration use the returned provider's name for `Provider`-based lookups. They would then request algorithms by the SUN provider name, or fail in unexpected ways. The result also depends on the default keystore type.

findings.title: New abstract method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: Adding the abstract `order()` method to a public SPI interface breaks any third-party CryptoProvider implementation at compile time and at runtime (AbstractMethodError). A `default` method returning a neutral value would avoid this.

findings.title: Duplicate providers with equal order are silently resolved
findings.body: The previous check that threw on multiple providers is removed. Two real providers on the classpath that both have order 200, for example default plus fips, now pick one arbitrarily, depending on classpath order, with only a debug log. A misconfigured deployment would then run with the wrong crypto provider and no error.
